title: document_manifest.json -- case document roster v0.5
description: The list of every document in a case and its processing status. This is a shared state file updated by multiple stages in sequence, not a single component's output -- it does not use the common output envelope. Update discipline: each stage adds only its own owner fields and never modifies fields it doesn't own (owner is documented per field below). This discipline is enforced structurally by the DAO's write_contract lock (see harness-guardrails P5), not just by convention. v0.5: first-class SEGMENT entries -- a document derived from a page-range of a physical parent (CASE_030's 240-page policy PDF was carved into DOC_004/005/006). document_role distinguishes 'physical' (a real raw file) from 'segment' (a derived page-range of a parent); a segment declares source_document_id, its page_map (logical printed page <-> parent PDF physical page), derivation_method, and derived_text_path, and MUST NOT fake independent OCR/classification metadata it never underwent. Lineage (parent exists, no self-parent/cycle, valid ranges, markers-match-declared-pages, parent processed before a segment is usable downstream) is enforced by the DAO's segment-lineage validator, which JSON Schema cannot express (it cannot read the processed text or compare entries to each other).

updated_at.description: owner: whichever stage last updated this file

document_role.description: owner: Case Intake / document-pipeline. 'physical' = a real raw file (data/raw/...). 'segment' = a derived page-range of a physical parent (source_document_id), e.g. CASE_030's DOC_004/005/006 carved from the 240-page policy. Absent is treated as 'physical' for backward compatibility.

policy_processing_role.description: owner: document-pipeline / policy-pipeline. What KIND of policy processing this document owes, declared explicitly. It used to be inferred from which artifacts happened to exist -- a document with a reference_table and no normalized clauses was assumed to be a table-only appendix, so simply not writing a clause contract exempted a document from ever having to produce one. Declaring the role does not by itself grant the exemption: the DAO verifies each declaration against the document's real source and its real children (a reference_table_only whose source contains normative narrative is refused; a segmented_parent needs genuine segments with processed text AND a parent-coverage contract, so one dummy child cannot exempt a parent from normalization). Required for every automated insurance_policy document at policy finalization.

source_document_id.description: owner: document-pipeline. For a segment: the physical parent document_id this segment was carved from. Must exist in this manifest and must not equal this document's own id (no self-parent); the lineage validator additionally forbids cycles. null/absent for a physical document.

derivation_method.description: owner: document-pipeline. How a segment's text was derived from its parent. Honest label -- a segment carved from a parent's already-extracted text is 'embedded_text_segment'/'page_extraction', NOT presented as if it underwent its own independent OCR.

derived_text_path.description: owner: document-pipeline. For a segment: the processed redacted text path (data/processed/CASE_XXX/DOC_XXX/redacted_text.md) built from the declared page range. null for a physical document (which uses redacted_text_path).

derived_text_sha256.description: owner: document-pipeline. SHA-256 of the exact derived redacted_text.md bytes for a segment. The DAO recomputes it on manifest writes, document-processing finalize, and normalized-policy writes so a segment cannot change after its lineage was approved.

page_map.description: owner: document-pipeline. For a segment: the explicit mapping from each of the segment's logical printed pages to the parent's PDF physical page. Distinguishes the printed page number that appears in <<<PAGE page=N>>> markers (logical_page) from the parent PDF's physical page index (source_physical_page), which can differ. The lineage validator checks that logical_page values match the segment's own redacted-text markers exactly.

segment_page_ranges.description: owner: document-pipeline. For a segment: the logical page ranges (possibly NON-contiguous -- DOC_004 is [{57,58},{118,119}]) this segment covers. A single {start,end} spanning a gap (e.g. 57-119) is wrong and is rejected by the lineage validator. Derivable from page_map but stated explicitly for readability and range-validity checks.

file_path.description: owner: Case Intake. Original raw path (data/raw/CASE_XXX/...) for a physical document; null for a segment (a segment has no raw file of its own).

file_format.description: owner: Case Intake. null for a segment (no file of its own).

file_size_bytes.description: owner: Case Intake. null for a segment (no file of its own).

pre_flagged_type.description: owner: Case Intake. Set when a document's type is already known at intake (e.g. an insurer-response document flagged during the source-ledger review) -- classification trusts this instead of running inference. null if not pre-flagged.

pages.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). Number of pages actually processed in this document entry. For a page-range run this may be smaller than source_total_pages.

source_total_pages.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). Immutable physical page count read from the original PDF container before any page-range extraction. Required by policy parent-coverage finalization so total pages cannot be self-declared by the policy agent. null for non-PDF inputs and segments.

source_pdf_sha256.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). SHA-256 of the immutable raw source file itself. Every segment carved from this parent binds its page mapping to this digest, so extracting from a DIFFERENT file -- or from a file that changed after the segments were derived -- is detectable rather than being an unverifiable claim about which PDF a page came from. null for non-PDF inputs and segments.

ocr_status.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). Initialized to pending by Case Intake.

ocr_quality.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). Copied from ocr_result_{document_id}.json's summary. null before OCR. Detail (uncertain-region list/positions, cross-validation outcome) lives only in ocr_result_{document_id}.json -- this manifest stays a lightweight roster.

uncertain_region_count.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). Sum of ocr_result_{document_id}.json's uncertain_regions for this document. null before OCR.

cross_validation_status.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). Result of P8's dual-path (OCR engine vs. blind vision-model read) cross-validation. Mirrors ocr_result_{document_id}.json's own cross_validation_status enum -- found out of sync for real when a real resolution's write was correctly rejected by schema validation (this file hadn't been updated when 'disagreed_resolved' was added there).

document_type.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). null before classification (or copied directly from pre_flagged_type when pre-flagged).

classification_confidence.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). null before classification; null (not 1.0) when pre-flagged, since no inference confidence applies.

extraction_method.description: owner: document-pipeline (checkpoint 1). non_text_image is human-verified visual evidence that must not be converted into synthetic page text.

downstream_disposition.description: owner: document-pipeline. expert_review_only excludes the document from text redaction, chunking, and automated downstream evidence use.

allOf.description: A segment declares its lineage: parent id, how it was derived, its derived text path, and its page ranges (all non-null). This is the schema half; the DAO's lineage validator checks the parent exists, no self-parent/cycle, ranges are valid, and the declared logical pages match the segment's redacted-text markers.
A physical document (document_role physical or absent) must have a real raw file_path -- it may not be null the way a segment's is.

page_range.description: An inclusive logical (printed) page range. start <= end enforced by the lineage validator, not the schema (schema can't compare two of its own fields).

page_map_entry.description: Maps one of a segment's logical printed pages to the parent PDF's physical page. logical_page is the number that appears in the segment's <<<PAGE page=N>>> markers (and in evidence-reference `page` values); source_physical_page is the parent PDF's 1-based physical page index, which may differ from the printed number. physical_page_sha256 and logical_page_evidence bind that mapping to the actual parent page rather than leaving it a declaration: a page offset asserted by a caller cannot be distinguished from a correct one unless the page's real content is hashed and its printed number independently read back.

physical_page_sha256.description: owner: document-pipeline. SHA-256 of the text extracted from the parent PDF's source_physical_page. Binds this mapping to the exact page it came from: re-running with a different PDF, or a shifted page offset, produces a different digest, so a wrong mapping cannot silently look consistent.

logical_page_evidence.description: owner: document-pipeline. The verbatim printed page marker found ON that physical page confirming its logical number (e.g. '12 / 240'). The page offset is only ever a CANDIDATE; this is the independent confirmation that the candidate was right. A page whose printed number cannot be read is not written with a guess -- extraction blocks for review.
